intro: You are standing in Amorium, an ancient city in Afyonkarahisar province whose story runs from the 2nd millennium BC to the 11th century AD. It was a major Byzantine military city, and it is remembered above all for the Arab sack of 838.
history: People lived here from Phrygian times. The city lay on the military road from Constantinople to Cilicia, and it was the birthplace of Emperor Theophilos. Then came 838. The Abbasids sacked Amorium, and it never fully recovered.
structure-1: Here is the Lower City Church. These church remains date from the early Christian period, in the lower city. Imagine the first believers gathering in this space.
structure-2: Now you are before the Great Church, the large church that served as the city's principal place of worship. This is where Amorium came together to pray.
structure-3: Look towards the Citadel. This fortified stronghold was built on high ground to protect the city, the last refuge when danger came.
structure-4: And here are the Excavated Buildings. In this area archaeologists continue their research, and the city is still slowly revealing its story.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Walls that once guarded this military city.
facts: Did you know? Amorium was one of Byzantium's largest military bases in Anatolia, and the home town of a ruling dynasty. In 838 the caliph al-Mu'tasim besieged and destroyed it. Officers captured during that siege refused to convert, and they were executed. Their story became one of the most famous tales of Christian history: the '42 Martyrs of Amorium', who entered the Byzantine calendar as the Forty-Two Martyrs of Amorium.
outro: This brings our tour of Amorium to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking with us, and enjoy your visit.
